subject.title: Subagent orchestration in cron isolated sessions: no reliable way to spawn, wait, and aggregate results

question: Should isolated cron remain a dispatcher-only fire-and-forget surface, or should OpenClaw own a narrow core fan-in continuation contract for cron parents?
rationale: The observable gap spans agent runtime lifecycle, cron delivery, and model-facing API design; the repository vision permits better agent harnesses but rejects heavy orchestration layers as a default architecture.

options.title: Document dispatcher-only cron
options.body: Document that isolated cron should dispatch one self-delivering subagent or use separate jobs, and state that parent fan-in is unsupported.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
options.body: Define a bounded cron-owned continuation or result-aggregation API with explicit lifecycle, timeout, storage, and delivery rules before implementation.

options.title: Defer to broader scheduler design
options.body: Keep this issue as context while a scheduler/event-chain proposal establishes whether fan-in belongs in a future product surface.

recommendation.title: Document dispatcher-only cron
recommendation.body: Document that isolated cron should dispatch one self-delivering subagent or use separate jobs, and state that parent fan-in is unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest available adjacent-history routing candidate, though the decision needs broader product ownership.
